title: ReCoG: Relational and Compact Context Graph Learning for Few-shot Molecular Property Prediction
claim: Supervised and context-aware approaches use context incompletely or redundantly; ours learns relational, compact context graphs for better predictions.
layout: 3 panels: wide top, two bottom; shared legend beneath
description: A three-panel comparison of few-shot molecular property prediction methods. The wide top panel, 'Supervision-driven FSMPP Methods', shows train and test tasks as stacked cards with query and support molecule sets. Both feed purple Molecular Encoder blocks that share weights through a dashed arrow. The encoders output predictions and losses. Two smaller bottom panels sit side by side. The left one, 'Context-aware FSMPP Methods', adds a context graph with triangle and pentagon nodes joined by red and blue edges. The right one, 'ReCoG (Ours)', has the same layout but highlights relational links, marks a pruned node with a red cross, and labels the L_rel and L_IB losses. Solid black arrows show information flow. Dashed orange and teal arrows show outer-loop and inner-loop updates. A legend runs along the bottom.
caption: The comparison of different FSMPP methods.
abstract: Few-shot molecular property prediction (FSMPP) is essential in drug discovery and materials design, where high-quality labeled data are often scarce and expensive to obtain. Despite the promising performance of existing methods, especially context-aware methods, they still face two-fold severe challenges with \textit{insufficient structural context modeling} \& \textit{redundant auxiliary context learning}, leading to inadequate context graph exploration and ineffective information utilization for effective molecule representation learning. To address these, in this paper, we propose a novel framework by learning on \textbf{\underline{Re}}lational and \textbf{\underline{C}}ompact c\textbf{\underline{o}}ntext \textbf{\underline{G}}raph, named \textbf{\method}, to comprehensively exploit the context graph for expressive molecular property prediction. Specifically, the proposed \method contains two core modules: a \textbf{(1) cross-property relational learning module} to better model the structural and relational context information, and a \textbf{(2) context graph information bottleneck module} to adaptively suppress irrelevant auxiliary signals for compact context information utilization, followed by a detailed theoretical demonstration regarding the importance of joint relational and compact knowledge extraction in context graphs.
